sections.title: Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
sections.description: This is a graduate-level seminar focused on select philosophical questions raised by artificial intelligence. Potential questions that might be covered include: How should AI reshape work, education, research, art, and human relationships, and what would be gained or lost if it replaced humans in those domains? What are the implications of AI for society, democracy, and the long-term future of humanity? Can (non-human) machines think, understand, or be conscious? Can AI systems mean things by what they say, be creative, or make genuine scientific discoveries? What are algorithms, and can we know things on the basis of systems whose workings we cannot explain? Could a machine be morally responsible or have moral status of its own? Drawing on philosophy of mind, epistemology, philosophy of science, metaphysics, and ethics, the course examines both what AI is and what it means for human life. Specific topics vary by semester. No technical background is required.
